topic.subject: science
topic.title: Control and coordination
topic.scope: neurons, reflex arc, brain, plant hormones and tropisms, animal hormones, feedback

misconceptions.statement: Nerve impulses are electrical currents like those in a copper wire.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the biological signal with physical electricity due to the use of terms like 'impulse' and 'current'.
misconceptions.fix: Nerve impulses are electrochemical signals involving the movement of ions across cell membranes, not the flow of electrons.

probe.question: Does a nerve impulse travel through a neuron at the same speed as electricity through a metal wire?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, it travels almost instantly like electricity.

misconceptions.statement: The brain is involved in every action we perform.
misconceptions.why: Students assume the brain is the 'boss' of the body and must consciously approve every movement.
misconceptions.fix: Reflex actions are involuntary responses processed by the spinal cord to ensure a faster reaction time without brain involvement.

probe.question: Why do we pull our hand away quickly when touching a hot object?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the brain thinks quickly and sends a command to the hand.

misconceptions.statement: Plants move towards light because they 'want' to grow towards it.
misconceptions.why: Students anthropomorphize plants, attributing human-like desires or intentions to biological growth processes.
misconceptions.fix: Tropisms are directional growth movements caused by the unequal distribution of auxins in response to environmental stimuli.

probe.question: Why does a potted plant kept in a dark room bend towards the window?
probe.wrong_answer: The plant wants to reach the sunlight to get food.

misconceptions.statement: Hormones are only needed when the body is sick or stressed.
misconceptions.why: Students associate 'hormones' with medication or extreme physiological changes like puberty, ignoring homeostatic functions.
misconceptions.fix: Hormones are chemical messengers constantly secreted by glands to regulate normal body functions like growth, metabolism, and blood sugar levels.

probe.question: Do healthy people have hormones in their blood all the time?
probe.wrong_answer: No, hormones are only released when the body needs to fight a disease or grow.
